titleText.en: Not to be confused with 'making money selling this stuff to OTHER people who think it works', which corporate accountants and actuaries have zero problems with.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish source manifest supplies only the truncated title text “No confundir con ”, which is preserved exactly rather than completed from the official English wording. The official English title text is preserved exactly. OCR merged the two words in ¿ES ASÍ?, omitted both checkmarks, read ESTARÍAN without its accent, and split the visibly wrapped MODER-/NO; the authored inventory follows the Spanish raster. GPS is an unchanged initialism and the two checkmarks are symbols, so all three are visible exclusions rather than Spanish word cards.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Disparatado describes an idea or claim that is unreasonable or makes little sense. It changes to disparatada, disparatados, or disparatadas to match what it describes.

example.es: Ese rumor parece disparatado.
example.en: That rumor seems absurd.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Funcionara is a hypothetical past form of funcionar. After si, it presents something as imagined rather than stating that it really works.

example.es: Si el plan funcionara, ahorraríamos tiempo.
example.en: If the plan worked, we would save time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: would be (helper before an ongoing action)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estarían is the plural “would” form of estar. Before a form ending in -ando or -iendo, it helps describe what people or things would be doing.

example.es: A esta hora estarían trabajando.
example.en: At this time they would be working.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to make a killing; to profit greatly (in ponerse las botas)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ponerse normally means putting something on or entering a state. In the informal expression ponerse las botas, the whole phrase can mean profiting or enjoying something in abundance.

example.es: Los vendedores se pusieron las botas durante la feria.
example.en: The sellers made a killing during the fair.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: boots; completes ponerse las botas, ‘to make a killing’ here
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Botas literally means boots. In ponerse las botas, it belongs to an informal fixed expression whose meaning comes from the phrase, not from footwear.

example.es: Con aquel encargo, se pusieron las botas.
example.en: They made a killing on that job.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Remota is the feminine singular form of remoto and matches a feminine noun such as visión.

example.es: La señal viene de una estación remota.
example.en: The signal comes from a remote station.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Radiestesia is the claimed practice of finding hidden water, minerals, or other things with a rod, pendulum, or similar object.

example.es: El artículo examinó la radiestesia.
example.en: The article examined dowsing.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In mystical claims, an aura is an invisible field said to surround a person or object. The ordinary word can also mean an atmosphere or impression.

example.es: La curandera afirmó que podía ver auras.
example.en: The healer claimed that she could see auras.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a distancia, ‘remotely’ or ‘at a distance’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Keep a with distancia in the fixed expression a distancia. It can describe something done from far away or without being physically present.

example.es: La entrevista se hizo a distancia.
example.en: The interview was conducted remotely.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: crystal; a crystal used in mystical claims
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here cristal names the mineral object associated with claims about ‘crystal energy,’ not ordinary window glass. Spanish often makes the relationship explicit with de, as in energía de los cristales.

example.es: La tienda vende cristales decorativos.
example.en: The shop sells decorative crystals.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Costes is especially common in Spain. Many other regions use costos for the same meaning.

example.es: Tenemos que reducir los costes.
example.en: We have to reduce costs.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: After costes, sanitarios means costs connected with healthcare. In other contexts, sanitario can refer to sanitation or a healthcare worker.

example.es: El informe compara los gastos sanitarios.
example.en: The report compares healthcare expenses.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In plan de negocio, de negocio classifies the plan as a business plan.

example.es: Prepararon un plan de negocio sencillo.
example.en: They prepared a simple business plan.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Afirmar can mean stating something confidently as true. It does not by itself say whether the claim is correct.

example.es: No basta con afirmar que funciona.
example.en: It is not enough to claim that it works.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Funcionan is the present-time plural form of funcionar.

example.es: Estas máquinas funcionan bien.
example.en: These machines work well.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Despiadadamente is built from despiadada, “ruthless,” plus -mente. It describes how an action or focus is pursued.

example.es: La empresa compitió despiadadamente.
example.en: The company competed ruthlessly.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Enfocado describes something directed toward a subject, goal, or result. It changes to enfocada, enfocados, or enfocadas to match what is described.

example.es: El curso está enfocado a principiantes.
example.en: The course is aimed at beginners.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: at; toward; introduces the target after enfocado
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After enfocado or enfocada, a can introduce the audience, goal, or result that something is aimed at.

example.es: La campaña está enfocada a los jóvenes.
example.en: The campaign is aimed at young people.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In business and economics, beneficios commonly means the money left as profit, not merely general advantages.

example.es: La compañía declaró beneficios este año.
example.en: The company reported profits this year.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What informal expression can mean making a lot of money or profiting greatly?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use ponerse las botas; in a money context, it means to make a killing or profit handsomely.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The literal words refer to putting on boots, but the fixed expression means getting an abundant benefit. The short attached part changes for the person: me pongo, te pones, se pone, nos ponemos, os ponéis, or se ponen las botas.

example.es: Con las ventas de verano, la tienda se puso las botas.
example.en: The shop made a killing on the summer sales.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens remotely or from far away?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a distancia after the activity or thing being described.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Keep a and distancia together, normally without an article between them. The expression can mean physically “at a distance” or, for work and communication, “remotely.”

example.es: Marta trabaja a distancia tres días por semana.
example.en: Marta works remotely three days a week.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the Spanish term for the claimed ability to perceive a distant or hidden target without ordinary senses?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Visión names sight or perception, and remota follows it in the feminine form. In paranormal contexts the two-word term refers to a claimed extrasensory ability, not ordinary viewing through a camera.

example.es: El documental examinó la llamada visión remota.
example.en: The documentary examined so-called remote viewing.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the Spanish name for the quantum theory of light and electrically charged particles?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Electrodinámica is a feminine noun, so cuántica takes the feminine singular ending -a. This is the conventional technical name, often abbreviated QED in English.

example.es: La electrodinámica cuántica hace predicciones muy precisas.
example.en: Quantum electrodynamics makes very precise predictions.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “business plan” in Spanish?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use plan de negocio; its plural is planes de negocio.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De negocio classifies what kind of plan it is. Plan changes to planes in the plural, while de negocio stays unchanged.

example.es: Necesitamos un plan de negocio claro.
example.en: We need a clear business plan.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is focused on or aimed at a particular goal or audience?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of estar, then enfocado, enfocada, enfocados, or enfocadas, followed by a and the target.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estar changes for the person, thing, and time. Enfocado changes to match what is being described, and a introduces the aim, audience, or intended result. A describing adverb can go before enfocado, as in muy enfocado.

example.es: El proyecto está enfocado a reducir residuos.
example.en: The project is aimed at reducing waste.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What “economic argument” is the comic using, and what makes the table funny?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: It argues that a genuinely useful phenomenon should attract profit-seeking organizations; the unchecked paranormal claims contrast with accepted physics that already has practical uses.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The table pairs each claim with a lucrative or strategic use. Relativity and quantum electrodynamics get checkmarks because they support real technologies, while the claimed paranormal effects do not. This is a skeptical rule of thumb, not a formal proof. The title-text joke adds an important distinction: companies can still profit by selling a belief to customers even when the claimed effect itself does not work.

applications.explanationEn: Al and final form the fixed connector that frames the conclusion reached after considering the table.
Significa carries the changed present form, while afirmar stays in its unchanged dictionary form as the action that this entails.

applications.exampleEs: CAPITALISMO MODERNO NO ESTÁ TAN DESPIADADAMENTE ENFOCADO
applications.explanationEn: Both moderno and enfocado use masculine singular -o because they describe capitalismo; the verb and modifiers simply stand between the noun and the second description.
Despiadada takes the adverb-forming ending -mente to describe the manner of the focus.
Tan goes immediately before the adverb despiadadamente and raises its degree to ‘so ruthlessly.’

applications.exampleEs: ESTÁ TAN DESPIADADAMENTE ENFOCADO A LOS BENEFICIOS
applications.explanationEn: Está and enfocado form the state, tan despiadadamente modifies its intensity and manner, and a los beneficios names the target of that focus.
